evidence: a-client-needs-tls-and-verifies-the-server: mysql_server.pp:14-18 build ssl_chain_file = /etc/mysql/ssl/p8test-chain.pem under the fixture (ssl_chain p8test-chain.pem), and server.cnf.epp:11 sets require_secure_transport = ON. The probe expects ERROR 3159 for a plaintext TCP login, a TLS session, VERIFY_CA success against exactly that chain file, and ERROR 2026 against an unrelated CA (ISRG Root X1). That is what those lines produce. mutates declares the account, the data-directory writes and the /run output. The action is a client exercise of the server's transport rule. The effect records the server's answers and the client's verification of the server certificate; it does not record a self-report. The node's error log (read after the run) has no entry from the action

purpose gap: Tested: MySQL 8.0 (not MariaDB) installed, active and enabled. The running server uses the managed config's datadir, TLS files, secure transport and bind 0.0.0.0 (ss also shows 0.0.0.0:3306). AppArmor's local include holds the paths and mysqld is confined in enforce mode while serving /srv/mysql. TCP clients must use TLS, and the server certificate verifies against the given chain (with an unrelated CA as the contrast). The TLS key is root:mysql 0640 in a 0750 directory and is readable by mysql, not by nobody. Root@localhost uses mysql_native_password, and a login without the password is refused. Gap: the class sets remove_default_accounts => true (mysql_server.pp:51). On the lab module (mysql::server::account_security) that removes root@127.0.0.1, root@::1, root@localhost.localdomain, root@<fqdn> and root@<hostname> as well as the anonymous accounts and the test database. The outcome row 'no anonymous account or test database remains' and the check root-needs-the-password-and-defaults-are-gone test only user='' and schema 'test'. The absence of any root account other than root@localhost is untested. This is the security-relevant half of the default-account removal: a root reachable over TCP from another host entry. The lab can check it with one read-only query (a read-only query on the applied node now lists only root@localhost besides mysql.infoschema/session/sys and the test account), and the outcomes table does not list it as uncovered
